Improvement: Give each rental a price, availability and a button
What the customer meets: Three long text blocks, with no price, no availability and no button. It isn't obvious the cards can be clicked.
Why it matters: A visitor ready to rent has no visible next step, so the rental journey ends on its first page.
Recommended fix: For each machine, show the price per hour or day, availability, and a "Check dates" button. Cut the text to 2–3 lines.

Improvement: Show stock, delivery and returns next to Add to cart
What the customer meets: Nothing near Add to cart says whether it's in stock, what delivery costs, when it arrives or how returns work.
Why it matters: These are the questions people need answered before paying. Without them, shoppers leave to check elsewhere, or buy and then ask.
Recommended fix: Add one line under the button: "In stock · Delivery $4.95, 2–3 days · 30-day returns".

Improvement: Move Add to cart up on phones
What the customer meets: On a phone, a long paragraph sits between the price and Add to cart. The button is about two screens down.
Why it matters: The main action is out of sight on the device most shoppers use.
Recommended fix: Put quantity and Add to cart right under the price. Cut the description to 3 lines with "Read more", and show key specs as bullets.

Improvement: Say what the shop is on the home page
What the customer meets: A banner photo and a filter column. Nothing says what the shop sells, for whom, or why buy here.
Why it matters: A first-time visitor has to work out what the site is. Those who don't, leave.
Recommended fix: Add a headline and one line over the banner ("Hand and power tools, delivered in 2 days"), plus 2–3 category shortcuts.

What the customer meets: You must sign in or register to buy. There's no guest checkout.
Why it matters: Being forced to create an account is one of the best-known reasons people abandon a cart, and new customers meet it on their very first order.
Recommended fix: Add "Continue as guest" next to sign-in, and offer to save an account after the order is placed.
Priority reason: Every new customer, at the last step before paying

Improvement: Add delivery, returns, privacy and about pages
What the customer meets: No page or footer link gives delivery, returns, privacy or about-us information.
Why it matters: A cautious buyer looks for these before trusting a shop with a card number.
Recommended fix: Add Delivery, Returns, Privacy and About pages. Link them in the footer and from the product and cart pages.

What the customer meets: The brand tag reads "Brand name 1" on every product checked.
Why it matters: Placeholder data makes the whole catalogue look unfinished.
Recommended fix: Show the real brand, or hide the tag when there isn't one.

Improvement: Close the phone menu after a choice
What the customer meets: After choosing Cart from the opened phone menu, the menu stays open and pushes the cart down the page.
Why it matters: Every menu use costs an extra tap, and the page looks broken.
Recommended fix: Close the menu once an item is chosen.
Priority reason: Every phone visitor using the menu

Improvement: Show delivery costs and Continue shopping in the cart
What the customer meets: No delivery cost, tax or estimated total before sign-in, and no "Continue shopping". Remove is an unlabelled red ×.
Why it matters: Costs that only appear late in checkout are a common reason to leave.
Recommended fix: Add "Delivery from $4.95" or "Delivery calculated next", a Continue shopping link, and a "Remove" label or tooltip.

Improvement: Make every message say what to do
What the customer meets: Messages don't say what to do: "Oeps, something went wrong.", and "Subject is required" while a subject is chosen.
Why it matters: A vague error leaves people guessing, and many simply stop.
Recommended fix: Every message names the field and the next step, next to the field, and none is generic. (Fixing two logged bugs removes the worst cases.)
Priority reason: Main journey; the bugs are logged separately

Improvement: Add contact details beside the form
What the customer meets: The form is the only way to reach the shop: no email, phone, address, hours or reply time.
Why it matters: Visitors check that a shop is reachable before they pay. With the form currently broken, there's no way to ask anything.
Recommended fix: Add an email address, a phone number, opening hours and "We reply within 1 working day" beside the form.
Priority reason: Trust; High while the form is broken

Improvement: Keep the cart across tabs and visits
What the customer meets: The cart lives only in the tab it was filled in. A new tab shows "The cart is empty" and no count.
Why it matters: Shoppers who compare products in tabs think their cart has gone.
Recommended fix: Keep a guest's cart across tabs and visits, for example saved in the browser for 30 days.
Priority reason: Shoppers who use tabs or come back later

Improvement: Fit the cart to a phone screen
What the customer meets: The cart table is wider than the screen. The page scrolls sideways and the remove button is cut off.
Why it matters: The last screen before paying looks broken on a phone.
Recommended fix: On phones, stack each cart line: name, then quantity and price, then remove.

Improvement: Suggest a matching add-on in the cart
What the customer meets: Nothing suggests an add-on. "Related products" shows similar tools, not what goes with this one.
Why it matters: A missed sale on almost every order: bits with a drill, a battery, a case.
Recommended fix: One quiet line in the cart: "Often bought with this: 10-piece drill bit set, $12.99 [Add]". Highlight only the price.

Improvement: Let renters pick dates and day rates
What the customer meets: Rental is by the hour only, up to 10 hours, with no date picker. "Out of stock" doesn't say when it's free. Nothing about delivery or an operator.
Why it matters: "Next week" can't be booked, and trades usually rent by the day.
Recommended fix: Add a date picker, day rates, "Available from …", and a line on delivery and operator.
Priority reason: Secondary journey, but a blocker for it

What the customer meets: The Sort box is blank. It doesn't say how the list is ordered.
Why it matters: Shoppers can't tell what order they're looking at.
Recommended fix: Show the current order as the default, e.g. "Sort by: Featured".

Improvement: Name each page in the browser tab
What the customer meets: Every page has the same tab title, "Practice Software Testing - Toolshop - v5.0 with bugs", including products, cart and checkout.
Why it matters: Tabs, bookmarks, history and search results all look the same.
Recommended fix: Name the page: "Cordless Drill 20V · Toolshop", "Cart (1) · Toolshop".
Priority reason: Polish, but it helps search too

Improvement: Align product names the same way
What the customer meets: Product names are right-aligned on some cards and left-aligned on others.
Why it matters: Small, but it reads as unpolished.
Recommended fix: Align all names the same way.

Improvement: Keep the chat button off the page's buttons
What the customer meets: The round chat button sits over the page and covers text and buttons as you scroll.
Why it matters: It can cover the very thing a shopper wants to tap.
Recommended fix: Make it smaller, move it to the bottom-right with a gap above the page's buttons, or hide it while scrolling.
